features.feature_value: Kept items that were “productive”/harmless; removed when “too inflammatory” or “random personal attacks.”
features.evidence_span: If things were too inflammatory or just random personal attacks I think I removed them.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states a content-based rule for keeping vs removing based on productivity/harmlessness versus inflammatory/personal attacks.

features.feature_value: Applied a line based on whether either post alone could encourage violence or illegal behavior.
features.evidence_span: determine if either of the posts alone would encourage violence or any type of illegal behavior.
features.rationale: The reflection directly describes the primary criterion they used when deciding whether to remove.

features.feature_value: Focused on whether statements could “incite a call to violence,” while allowing broader speech.
features.evidence_span: I just focused on whether the statements could incite a call to violence.
features.rationale: They state that incitement to violence was the governing threshold for their decisions.

features.feature_value: Allowed people to voice beliefs but would not approve pairs with racial slurs/bad words or that were too “off putting.”
features.evidence_span: not use racial slurs or bad words... if one seemed really off putting I wouldnt approve the pair.
features.rationale: The participant names specific disallowed content types and a qualitative “off putting” boundary.

features.feature_value: Did not allow profanity or “intense mockery,” but allowed differences of opinion; “Respect is the key word.”
features.evidence_span: If an profanity was used or intense mockery I did not allow them. If they were just differences of oppinion I went ahead and let them go through. Respect is the key word here.
features.rationale: They provide a clear rule distinguishing disrespectful/profanity content from acceptable disagreement.

features.feature_value: Evaluated whether the opinion was “sound” regardless of agreement; deleted opinions rooted in anger as less productive.
features.evidence_span: I just paid attention to how sound the opinion was regardless of if I agreed with it. Some opinions seemed primarily based in anger, and I chose to delete those because they seemed less productive.
features.rationale: Their comparison/selection method emphasizes soundness over stance and uses anger as a deletion cue.

features.feature_value: Decisions were driven by “severity of the language/tone” and “the way they were framed.”
features.evidence_span: The severity of the language/tone used in the posts, as well as the way they were framed.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly points to tone/severity and framing as the influential cues.

features.feature_value: Described feeling “sad,” and assigned blame broadly to the internet/social media; still let content pass if some truth existed in both statements.
features.evidence_span: The feeling I felt was "This is sad"... If both statements had some truth... I let it pass.
features.rationale: They combine affect (“sad”) with a rationale for passing decisions based on perceived truth across statements.
